description: Reviewed difference classes between astgen 1.10.6 (TypeScript 6) type maps and the native binary (TypeScript 7). A class not listed here fails lib/typemap/diff.mjs. Normalizations (union and object member order, quote style, typeof against a signature) live in lib/typemap/canon.mjs with their own tests and need no entry.

classes.reason: typescript-go returns no type for the identifier of a type reference, so the identifier takes the type of its enclosing reference (getTypeFromTypeNode), as the brief requires. TypeScript 6 gave the identifier the declared type (Promise<T>) and kept the longer string at the shared offset. The reference itself is typed identically.

TypeScript 6 printed the type of a CommonJS module or require() result as `typeof module.exports` or `typeof import("./m")`; TypeScript 7 writes the structure of the same type. The names inside are the same; only the printer chose differently. Checked on the JSDoc fixture (r17-jsdoc.js) and node-express-boilerplate.

The reverse of typeof-vs-structure: TypeScript 7 names a value with typeof where TypeScript 6 wrote its structure (1,253 keys over the corpus, 0.02%; checked on the CommonJS fixtures: `typeof import(".")` for a module that TypeScript 6 printed as `typeof module.exports`).

The same type with a different import("...") path (8,634 keys, 0.16%). TypeScript 7 resolves package entry points through `exports` and writes the path it reached; astgen normalizes the specifier relative to the file in both.
Equal apart from parentheses around a function type in a type argument (`Meta<(<E>(a: E) => any)>` against `Meta<<E>(a: E) => any>`, 40 keys). A printer difference between the versions.
TypeScript 6 renames a type parameter that shadows another (T_1); TypeScript 7 writes T (197 keys). Same type, a different name for the parameter.
Equal apart from `| undefined` on an optional property (1,724 keys, 0.03%): the two versions print optionality differently under exactOptionalPropertyTypes.
tsgo types `export default X` and `export =` expressions; TypeScript 6 produced no type there (1,283 keys over 14 projects). More information, not a disagreement.
